text:
alex: Quick question — running into a compatibility problem for KV cache layout when we roll quantized model variants across hosted/dedicated/private. Need a minimal contract for probe + invalidation.

maria: Can you sketch the failure? is this cache corruption or just layout mismatch that yields wrong embeddings?

alex: Layout mismatch. Old runtime expects sequential keys `pref:<tenant>:<model>:<seq>`; quantized variant switched to chunked keys which makes lookups return stale prefixes. Symptoms: inference returns fallback tokens then high latency while trying to rebuild cache.

chao: Ugh. This is the classic schema-evolution problem. Two ideas:
- capability discovery at connect time (runtime advertises supported kv_layout versions)
- conservative invalidation when model variant changes (ttl + forced namespace bump)

olivia: Both are OK, but private deployments (air-gapped) won't talk to control plane for capability negotiation. We need a local-only fallback for them.

chao: Right. Proposal A (control-plane-first): store model capability manifest in control-plane + push to runtime on rollout. Runtime accepts `manifest.v` and if it sees a layout delta it either invalidates or linearizes old keys.
Proposal B (probe-first/minimal): runtime exposes tiny probe API that client (or gateway) can call before traffic: `POST /probe` -> `{ "kv_layout": "v1" }` and runtime returns supported set. If mismatch, client chooses model variant or triggers eviction.

alex: I like probe-first for hosted + dedicated because it's simple. For private, we need an option to embed the manifest in the deployment bundle.

maria: Thoughts on safety? forced invalidation could be expensive across large tenants. Maybe we should support a namespace token that is bumped on incompatible changes (`ns_token = sha(model+layout+version)`), so invalidation is just a namespace switch.

chao: Yes — namespace-token approach is cheap. You can do key prefixing by token: `ns:<token>:pref:...`. Old keys remain but won't be referenced. Garbage collection can be async.

olivia: Security question: the probe endpoint must not leak tenant info or allow enumeration. Make it auth-only and ensure it never exposes any tenant-specific keys. Probe should return only capability flags, e.g. `{"kv_layout": "v2", "supports_namespace_token": true}`.

alex: Sample minimal probe payload I had in mind:```json
{
  "client": "gateway",
  "model_variant": "redwood/quantized-x86-v2",
  "expected_kv_layout": "v1"
}
```runtime reply could be:```json
{
  "kv_layout": "v2",
  "namespace_token": "sha256:...",
  "action": "switch|invalidate|no-op"
}
```
Note: these are drafts, obviously.

maria: +1, but I prefer `action` enums: `NO_OP`, `BUMP_NAMESPACE`, `FORCE_INVALIDATE`. Avoid freeform strings.

chao: Implementation tradeoffs: keep probe in runtime binary to avoid control-plane complexity. But then dedicated/hosted can optionally forward to control-plane for rollout-wide coordination. Private gets manifest baked into the deployment and runs the same local probe logic.

olivia: Also add a flag `opt_in_probe_on_startup` for private installs. Default false. People can enable for staged rollouts to avoid surprises.

alex: Action items: I'll open an RFC with: probe API spec (fields + enum), namespace-token scheme, GC guidance, and a migration checklist for existing models.

maria: I'll add an e2e test scenario: quantized switch -> namespace bump -> no cache collisions and monitor token presence in traces.

chao: I'll prototype a tiny probe server in runtime and share PoC PR.

deploy-bot: Deploy successful: runtime/probe-poc -> staging (rev b4c2) :rocket:

alex: Thanks all — posting RFC link shortly and tagging folks for review. :memo:
